title: Uniform machine-code system
statement: A uniform machine-code system consists of an effective code for deterministic two-work-tape machines over binary symbols, together with a finite binary-input simulator and a natural-number degree. For every code, input, and time bound, the simulator decides whether the decoded machine outputs the one-bit word $[1]$ on that input within the given bound: in the affirmative case it outputs $[1]$, and otherwise it outputs $[0]$. In either case its computation takes exactly the prescribed time bound $d(|\alpha|+|x|+t+1)^d$, where $d$ is the degree and $\alpha,x,t$ are the code, input, and bound; the code system also includes a finite machine computing the serialization of each decoded machine, with some time bound depending on input length.
hypotheses_covered: The inherited code and decoder are total and decode strings with the stated padding property.
A finite binary machine computes the serialization of each decoded machine within its specified time bound.
A single natural-number simulator degree is fixed.
For every code, input, and time bound, bounded acceptance implies output [true] in the stated polynomial number of steps.
For every code, input, and time bound, failure of bounded acceptance implies output [false] in the same stated polynomial number of steps.
